While a range of topological and geometric metrics have been explored, they are typically analyzed in isolation, and the connections between them remain largely unknown. In this paper, we present Unified Topological Signatures (UTS) for characterizing the structure of embedding spaces. We evaluate our method across a wide range of text embedding models and retrieval datasets, finding that it outperforms individual metrics in downstream performance prediction. Through several experiments, we demonstrate that the signatures characterize embedding spaces more accurately, improve the prediction of model-specific properties and biases, and reveal novel insights into representational similarity that challenge the global claims of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.

Information Retrieval.title: HASTE: Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for Generative Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Generative recommendation models have shown promising results by representing items as semantic IDs and generating these IDs autoregressively. We introduce an approach showing that explicitly incorporating hierarchical and attribute-level supervision into generative recommendation can simultaneously improve training efficiency and long-tail recommendation performance. Existing approaches typically optimize semantic ID prediction with a standard causal cross-entropy objective, which does not explicitly exploit the hierarchical structure of semantic IDs and can require substantial training to learn effective item representations. Moreover, data-sparse tail items often suffer from poor representations due to limited supervision, resulting in weaker long-tail recommendation performance. We address these challenges with HASTE (Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for generaTive rEcommendation), a unified training framework that introduces hierarchical and attribute-specific supervision. HASTE's Hierarchical Loss explicitly exploits the multi-level structure of semantic IDs, providing supervision at each level of the item hierarchy and substantially accelerating training convergence. Its Attribute-Specific Losses encourage the model to preserve fine-grained item attributes, leveraging the language model's inherent semantic knowledge to improve representations and recommendations for tail items. We extensively evaluate HASTE on a fashion recommendation benchmark and across multiple domains of the Amazon dataset. HASTE improves recommendation performance across datasets and item-frequency regimes. Notably, the Hierarchical Loss achieves approximately 2x faster convergence than the standard causal cross-entropy objective, substantially improving training efficiency while maintaining strong recommendation quality.

Information Retrieval.title: A Reduction-Driven Local Search for the Generalized Independent Set Problem
Information Retrieval.summary: The Generalized Independent Set (GIS) problem extends the classical maximum independent set problem by incorporating profits for vertices and penalties for edges. This generalized problem has been identified in diverse applications in fields such as forest harvest planning, competitive facility location, social network analysis, and even machine learning. However, solving the GIS problem in large-scale, real-world networks remains computationally challenging. In this paper, we explore data reduction techniques to address this challenge. We first propose 14 reduction rules that can reduce the input graph with rigorous optimality guarantees. We then present a reduction-driven local search (RLS) algorithm that integrates these reduction rules into the pre-processing, the initial solution generation, and the local search components in a computationally efficient way. The RLS is empirically evaluated on 278 graphs arising from different application scenarios. The results indicates that the RLS is highly competitive -- For most graphs, it achieves significantly superior solutions compared to other known solvers, and it effectively provides solutions for graphs exceeding 260 million edges, a task at which every other known method fails. Analysis also reveals that the data reduction plays a key role in achieving such a competitive performance.
Information Retrieval.comment: We corrected several errors in the proof, including incorrect signs in the exchange inequalities

Information Retrieval.title: From Conceptual EneMonIE to an Executable Backend: A Modular Architecture for Energy Information Extractionand Grounded Question Answering
Information Retrieval.summary: The original EneMonIE proposal describes a Web-based semantic system for continuously monitoring energy trends through targeted information extraction from heterogeneous online media. This article presents EneMonIE-Backend, an implementation-derived redesign that converts that conceptual pipeline into a modular, executable, and application-independent backend. The architecture separates five concerns: data sources, acquisition and normalization, semantic processing, knowledge organization, and persistent storage. It operationalizes configurable connectors for RSS feeds, URL collections, arXiv, social-media JSON files, and open-data CSV files; it also introduces question-driven Web search and scraping. Relevant documents pass through energy categorization, named entity recognition, temporal and event extraction, source sensitive sentiment analysis, and extractive summarization. The resulting semantic representations support entity co-occurrence graphs, cross-document interlinking, cluster-level information fusion, and relational persistence in SQLite. Three grounded question-answering paths are exposed at the backend level: live Web evidence, the stored corpus, and selected configured resources. Answer generation uses a language model when configured and otherwise falls back to deterministic extractive output. Unlike the original proposal, the presented architecture deliberately excludes the user-interface and server-side application layers, allowing the semantic core to be embedded in different applications. A deterministic smoke validation confirms relevance filtering, persistence, clustering, evidence retrieval, and document deletion. The work provides a reproducible architectural basis for future evaluation on larger multilingual energy corpora.

Information Retrieval.title: Tracing Money Flows in the Multi-Token Cryptocurrency Network
Information Retrieval.summary: Tracing money flows in cryptocurrency transaction networks is challenging because funds can move across accounts, transactions, and token layers. We propose a transaction-aware graph in which nodes represent account--asset states within transactions, while edges encode observed transfers, inferred asset transformations, and temporal inter-transaction sequences. Applied to Aave borrow--repay flows, we compare graph construction and edge-pruning strategies and extract shortest paths using a heuristic weighting. Our results reveal a trade-off between reachability and interpretability and uncover frequent token sequences underlying how borrowed assets are transformed before repayment. This work lays a foundation for general, interpretable multi-token flow tracing.
Information Retrieval.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, 19 references, 15th International Conference on Complex Networks and Their Applications

Information Retrieval.title: WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat
Information Retrieval.summary: Generative retrieval (GR) offers a promising paradigm for industrial search by unifying candidate generation within an autoregressive framework. However, its effectiveness is limited by two key challenges. First, existing Semantic ID (SID) tokenizers struggle to incorporate collaborative signals while maintaining effective codebook utilization, limiting their ability to distinguish items and achieve high-quality retrieval. Second, existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods suffer from severe reward sparsity under exact SID matching, leaving many sampled trajectories without effective learning signals and hindering preference optimization. To address these challenges, we propose WeGR, a unified generative retrieval framework consisting of two complementary components. Specifically, the Collaborative and Collapse-free Tokenizer (CoCo-VAE) incorporates query-to-item and item-to-item collaborative signals while mitigating codebook collapse through codebook refresh and complementary regularization, enabling more informative and balanced SID representations. Building upon these SIDs, Dynamic Horizon Policy Optimization (DHPO) progressively expands both reward evaluation and policy optimization horizons, reducing learning difficulty while leveraging behavioral reward signals at different levels of the SID hierarchy, without relying on auxiliary reward models. Extensive offline experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of WeGR in improving retrieval and ranking performance. Moreover, a two-month online A/B test in WeChat E-commerce Search demonstrates relative improvements of 2.539% in orders, 1.508% in click-through rate, and 1.381% in conversion rate, while reducing online CPU and GPU usage by 25.5% and 26.1%, respectively. The system has been successfully deployed across multiple search scenarios in WeChat, serving billions of users, generating tens of millions of PVs daily.

Information Retrieval.title: Decision-Oriented Recommendation Reranking: An Empirical Study of Its Promise and Limitations
Information Retrieval.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for recommendation reranking, but their use introduces an important trade-off between recommendation quality and serving efficiency. We investigate whether decision-oriented systems provide a useful alternative when the reranking task is fundamentally a structured choice among predefined candidate items. Specifically, we conduct a controlled empirical study of two decision-oriented systems, TypeSafe Jev and OpenAI Decisions, for recommendation reranking. Across three Amazon Reviews domains and four candidate-set sizes, we compare these systems against recommendation-specific models and pointwise and listwise LLM-based rerankers, systematically evaluating recommendation effectiveness, candidate-order robustness, and efficiency and scalability. Our results reveal that Jev frequently achieves a favorable quality--latency trade-off, offering competitive recommendation effectiveness at substantially lower observed latency than stronger LLM-based alternatives. Overall, our findings suggest that specialization for decision-making does not inherently guarantee superior recommendation quality or robustness. Instead, the practical value of decision-oriented inference depends on implementation-specific characteristics and application requirements. These findings motivate further investigation of decision-oriented systems for recommendation and other ranking tasks with structured output spaces.

Information Retrieval.title: KNN Implementation Details Can Dramatically Change Performance: An Example from Cover Trees
Information Retrieval.summary: Nearest neighbor search algorithms are widely used and have a long history, but we find that key implementation details are seldom reviewed in articles about them. These details can materially impact performance, and thus change the conclusions one makes about a given algorithm's superiority. In this article, we highlight these impacts by reviewing the Cover Tree as an example, producing RustKNN, a unified Rust implementation of three construction variants of the Cover Tree with three query modes. Our analysis reveals: (1) the optimal query strategy depends on $k$ and on the dataset (single-tree search is fastest at $k{=}1$ on three of our four largest datasets, while dual-tree search is fastest at $k{\ge}5$ on the three largest), and choosing the wrong query mode can cost up to a $7.5\times$ factor in runtime; (2) the cover tree base parameter, set to 2 in theory and 1.3 in practice, is not a safe default for dual-tree search: 1.3 is optimal on only one of seven datasets, and on covtype it is $1.6\times$ slower than the optimum; (3) among five micro-optimizations, only early-exit distance computation has a consistent effect, and that effect grows with dimension (none at $d{=}32$, $1.31\times$ at $d{=}54$, and $1.49\times$ at $d{=}784$); and (4) all-nearest-neighbor and held-out benchmarks yield different implementation rankings. All main timing tables report medians over 20 independent allocations with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. RustKNN is open source at https://github.com/CrowdStrike/RustKNN.
Information Retrieval.comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Track on Evaluations and Datasets

Information Retrieval.title: Comparing GenAI to Machine Learning and Manual Review for eDiscovery
Information Retrieval.summary: Keeling et al. [Keeling2026Generative] report on a case study recently conducted by Redgrave LLP in which they assert that Relativity's Generative AI Review tool (aiR) achieved 88% recall while Relativity Assisted Learning (RAL), its machine-learning tool, achieved 64% recall. These results are not comparable because the methods employed have different objectives, because of inter-assessor disagreement, and because they represent different recall-precision and cost-benefit trade-offs. Our analysis of the Redgrave data indicates that, when these differences are taken into account, aiR and manual review are comparable. Furthermore, established machine-learning models employing Continuous Active Learning (CAL) show state-of-the-art effectiveness, and superior efficiency, when trained only on a sample of 2,000 first-pass-reviewer responsiveness determinations.

Information Retrieval.title: From Volpiano to Pixels: 30,000 Lines of OMR Ground Truth for Medieval Chant
Information Retrieval.summary: Optical music recognition (OMR) for medieval chant lacks training data linking manuscript images to musical symbols across notational families. Using existing Volpiano transcriptions from the Cantus Database, we created 30,567 image-target pairs from ten sources in eleven exports, including 339 verse fragments. Their target sequences contain 1,952,143 tokens. The pipeline locates staff systems, infers clefs and maps known pitches to staff positions. Six detector families handle the different layouts and notations. Where heuristics failed, two small U-Nets learned staff lines and clef letters from manual annotations. Reviews of sampled export lines found zero to four pitch or clef errors, but used different error definitions and do not provide a uniform audit of the corpus. A CRNN trained from scratch achieved a symbol error rate of 9.6 % on 3,086 test lines. The earlier model, trained mainly on Austrian sources of the 15th and 16th centuries, scored 45.3 %. In three separate training runs, each excluding one manuscript, error rates on the excluded manuscript were 21.5-31.0 %. Model-assisted alignment recovered a further 2,686 lines.

Information Retrieval.title: Separating Prompt Harmfulness from Interaction Safety via Partial Generation
Information Retrieval.summary: LLM-based information systems need safety guardrails. Most guardrails classify the prompt alone. If the prompt looks harmful, the system rejects it before any answer is generated. This is costly. Many rejected prompts would have received a safe response. Users lose help they should have received from the information system. This cost grows as conversational and generative search becomes common. Prompt-level labels treat harm as a property of the query. But harm depends on what the model actually writes. Existing input-output guards do look at responses. But they judge a finished response, so the decision comes after full generation. However, we observe that safety of model interaction with the input prompt can be inferred early with only partial output. So the system can start generating, watch the partial response, and stop only if it turns harmful. We test this idea in three steps. First, we build a dataset of 41,944 prompt-response pairs with seven open weights LLMs from three families: Llama, Gemma, and Qwen. Second, we show that prompt harmfulness and interaction safety differ. Prompt labels and response labels agree on only 50.46\% of items (Cohen's $κ$ = 0.06). Of the prompts that make any model respond harmfully, only 3.5\% do so for all seven LLMs. Third, we show that partial responses carry most of the signal. Fine-tuned classifiers predict response-level harm well (best AUPRC 0.885, F1 0.807). About one third of the response tokens recover almost full-response AUPRC.

Information Retrieval.title: Agent-OM: Leveraging LLM Agents for Ontology Matching
Information Retrieval.summary: Ontology matching (OM) enables semantic interoperability between different ontologies and resolves their conceptual heterogeneity by aligning related entities. OM systems currently have two prevailing design paradigms: conventional knowledge-based expert systems and newer machine learning-based predictive systems. While large language models (LLMs) and LLM agents have revolutionised data engineering and have been applied creatively in many domains, their potential for OM remains underexplored. This study introduces a novel agent-powered LLM-based design paradigm for OM systems. With consideration of several specific challenges in leveraging LLM agents for OM, we propose a generic framework, namely Agent-OM (Agent for Ontology Matching), consisting of two Siamese agents for retrieval and matching, with a set of OM tools. Our framework is implemented in a proof-of-concept system. Evaluations of three Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative (OAEI) tracks over state-of-the-art OM systems show that our system can achieve results very close to the long-standing best performance on simple OM tasks and can significantly improve the performance on complex and few-shot OM tasks.

Information Retrieval.title: EHR-Bench: A Chinese Multi-Task Benchmark for Recruitment AI
Information Retrieval.summary: Recruitment applications span diverse operations, from drafting job descriptions and interpreting queries to organizing profiles, assessing fit, and recommending candidates and jobs. Systematic LLM evaluation therefore requires task coverage that reflects this range of business needs. We introduce EHR-Bench, an open Chinese benchmark comprising twelve tasks across six capability families and five recruitment scenarios. The tasks cover generation, extraction, classification, retrieval, semantic similarity, and reciprocal ranking within one evaluation framework. An internal recruitment dataset guides task definitions, the occupation taxonomy and sampling targets, output requirements, and scoring protocols. Following these specifications, we construct 8,336 task instances from public materials and controlled augmentation, with source-aware expert review and documented provenance. We evaluate twelve LLMs through task-level, capability-level, and aggregate comparisons. Closely ranked models exhibit distinct task strengths, and performance varies across input sources, reference evidence, and candidate pools. Five shared models retain the same observed Overall ordering on a private operational reference, with variation in capability and task correspondence. EHR-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for systematic model assessment, task-specific model selection, and further research on LLMs for recruitment. The project repository is available at https://github.com/EhrBench/EHR-Bench.

Information Retrieval.title: FindRec: Stein-Guided Entropic Flow for Multi-Modal Sequential Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Modern recommendation systems face significant challenges in processing multimodal sequential data, particularly in temporal dynamics modeling and information flow coordination. Traditional approaches struggle with distribution discrepancies between heterogeneous features and noise interference in multimodal signals. We propose \textbf{FindRec}~ (\textbf{F}lexible unified \textbf{in}formation \textbf{d}isentanglement for multi-modal sequential \textbf{Rec}ommendation), introducing a novel "information flow-control-output" paradigm. The framework features two key innovations: (1) A Stein kernel-based Integrated Information Coordination Module (IICM) that theoretically guarantees distribution consistency between multimodal features and ID streams, and (2) A cross-modal expert routing mechanism that adaptively filters and combines multimodal features based on their contextual relevance. Our approach leverages multi-head subspace decomposition for routing stability and RBF-Stein gradient for unbiased distribution alignment, enhanced by linear-complexity Mamba layers for efficient temporal modeling. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate FindRec's superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines, particularly in handling long sequences and noisy multimodal inputs. Our framework achieves both improved recommendation accuracy and enhanced model interpretability through its modular design. The implementation code is available anonymously online for easy reproducibility~\footnote{https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/FindRec}.

Information Retrieval.title: From a Large-Scale Teacher to Efficient Multimodal Students for Search Relevance Prediction
Information Retrieval.summary:
Relevance prediction between user queries and items is a fundamental component of e-commerce search systems. Traditionally, high-quality relevance labels are obtained through human judgment, which is reliable but expensive, slow, and difficult to scale. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) enable automated relevance judgment at scale, achieving performance comparable to human annotators. However, such systems often rely on large commercial LLMs with complex prompts, resulting in high inference costs and limited throughput.
  In this work, we propose a framework that bridges this gap by distilling a high-performing LLM-based relevance judgment system into efficient multimodal student models. We first curate a small, high-quality human-annotated dataset to serve as ground truth. Using this dataset, we develop a reliable LLM-as-a-judge pipeline through careful prompt engineering and iterative refinement. This pipeline is then used to generate large-scale relevance labels, which serve as training data for compact multimodal models. Our distilled models achieve performance close to the teacher system while significantly improving latency, cost, and scalability. This approach enables practical deployment of high-quality relevance prediction systems in production environments.

Information Retrieval.title: Open Tabular Insight Extraction: Where Do We Stand, and Where Should We Go?
Information Retrieval.summary: Democratizing access to the knowledge held in large corpora of tables such as data lakes is emerging as a central research challenge. Research in this space is advancing and broadening in scope, increasingly supplying the components to satisfy a person's insight need end-to-end. Yet these efforts remain fragmented across communities that frame the problem under their own conventions, such as table question answering, text-to-SQL, and data analysis agents, with works six times as likely to cite within the same task label as across labels. To bring these communities onto common ground, we establish a holistic framework for this pursuit, which we refer to as Open Tabular Insight Extraction (OpenTI). We formalize OpenTI from first principles around the analytical knowledge a person needs, the procedure for deriving it from a corpus of tables, and how well a result serves the person who sought it. In doing so we consolidate frameworks and terminology across information retrieval, natural language processing, machine learning, databases, and human-computer interaction, and apply this grounding in a systematic review and analysis of systems and benchmarks that work towards OpenTI. We find that current systems do not cover the end-to-end scope of OpenTI, mainly focusing on the analysis itself, and that benchmarks are largely unfit for evaluations in an open setting as inputs presuppose knowledge of tables, and validation mechanisms do not match the setup. Finally, we distill a research agenda towards OpenTI systems, evaluation, and interaction paradigms that surface the insights users need. An interactive companion to our paper is available at https://open-tabular-insight-extraction.github.io.

Information Retrieval.title: ARMED: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Medication Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Medication recommendation requires jointly considering diagnoses, comorbidities, longitudinal patient history, and treatment interactions. Although recent retrieval-augmented generation approaches using language models have shown promise for clinical recommendation, most existing systems rely on fixed retrieval pipelines that cannot adapt to diverse clinical retrieval scenarios and may introduce noisy or irrelevant evidence. We propose ARMED, an adaptive clinical RAG framework that dynamically expands retrieval according to retrieval sufficiency and current-admission relevance. ARMED first observes the initial retrieval outcome and selectively performs supplementary or fallback multi-query retrieval when additional evidence is needed. The framework also incorporates a relevance gate that activates only clinically relevant same-patient history and organizes retrieved evidence into structured query-level clinical evidence. Experiments on MIMIC-IV demonstrate that ARMED consistently outperforms previous static retrieval baselines and improves overall medication recommendation quality. By combining locally runnable small language models with adaptive retrieval, ARMED supports medication recommendation without relying on external language model APIs or task-specific fine-tuning.

Information Retrieval.title: Tackling the Modality Inhibitance Effect with Wavelet-based Modality Integration in Multi-modal Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Harnessing rich modality features has recently gained prominence in multi-modal recommendation systems (MRSs). To delineate user modality preferences, existing works focus on modality fusion, which can be achieved via attentive summation or concatenation. In this work, we introduce the modality inhibitance effect - a phenomenon which limits existing MRSs when these models transit from dual-modal to tri-modal configurations resulting in significant performance degradation. In particular, apart from the modal-specific contamination encapsulated in the newly introduced modality, the inclusion of new features results in excessive informational redundancy, thereby severely impeding effective integration within current approaches. To address the modality inhibitance effect, we propose a new multi-scale modality wavelet (MMWave) multi-modal recommender, which aims to fully capitalize on essential modality features and suppress modal-specific noise. This is acheived by employing wavelet decomposition from a multi-scale (time \& frequency) perspective, ensuring that only essential (non-redundant) features of each modality are extracted. We then account for the latent associations between item modality features by designing a new structure-aware multi-modal graph learning module that captures high-order latent structural information pertaining to items. To modulate the relative contributions of modality features and achieve effective integration, we then propose a new adaptive modality regulator component that employs a new cross-weight integration strategy. Experiments conducted on four real-world datasets validate the efficacy of our proposed model. The source code for this work has been made publicly available at https://github.com/kennethorq/MMWave.
Information Retrieval.comment: Published in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE) 2026

Information Retrieval.title: Recall Begets Recall: Recurrent Memory Ranking for Personalized LLMs
Information Retrieval.summary: Memory ranking is the stage in personalized Large Language Models (LLMs) that decides which of the candidate memories returned by a retriever enter the limited context, so that the answer is grounded in the right parts of the user's history. Existing memory rankers operate in a single pass, scoring each candidate once against the raw query and cutting the ranked list at a fixed top-K. The single pass misses memories that the answer needs but that look unrelated to the query on their own, and the fixed cut ignores how many memories the query needs. To address both problems, we propose ReMind, a memory ranker that runs as a recurrent and self-terminating loop, following the cognitive theory of memory search: each recalled item joins the cue for the next recall (compound cueing), and recall stops once enough has been collected for the task (metamemory monitoring). For compound cueing, ReMind adds the top-ranked memory to the query context at each step and reranks the remaining candidates under the expanded cue, so that each recall makes the cue more specific and later steps look for what is still missing rather than for what merely resembles the query. For metamemory monitoring, a sufficiency predictor estimates at each step whether the collected memories are enough to answer the query and stops the loop once they are, so that the number of selected memories adapts to each query. Experiments on public benchmarks show that ReMind achieves the best results compared to state-of-the-art memory rankers.

Information Retrieval.title: UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary:
Semantic-ID-based generative recommendation unifies retrieval and ranking through autoregressive decoding but differs structurally from discriminative models, which can directly access rich target-item side features. The attributes are compressed into a finite codebook during quantization, while the target item remains undetermined during decoding and its features cannot be looked up. This target-side feature vacuum weakens generation at each semantic-ID level through high conditional entropy and cascading errors, and final ranking through missing target-side feature crossing.
  Existing methods interact with candidate representations or generate discrete attribute tokens, but none reconstructs a continuous target-side representation inside decoding to support both stepwise generation and ranking. We propose TacGR (Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation). Before decoding each codeword, TacGR anticipates a continuous target-side feature vector and crosses it with the semantic prefix and user behavior sequence inside the decoder. The crossed representation conditions current-level generation and is directly used for ranking.
  Continuous-vector regression risks a learnable target collapsing with its prediction and prediction noise propagating into generation through attention. TacGR addresses these challenges with a semantic-anchoring auxiliary tower and a unidirectional visibility mask, respectively. For extremely long industrial behavior histories, it introduces gated convolutional denoising to suppress noise and adapts the pyramid memory funnel to reduce inference cost. Offline experiments on a large-scale Lazada dataset show significant gains over OneRec, UniRec, and UniSGR. Online A/B testing improves IPV, Order, and GMV by 0.79%, 5.55%, and 3.09%, respectively.

Information Retrieval.title: OT-FlowRec: Optimal Transport-Guided Multi-Bridge Flow for Multimodal Sequential Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: E-commerce user preferences evolve dynamically within sessions, exhibiting concurrent and multi-centric interest distributions. While existing multimodal sequential recommendation methods leverage global attention to compress historical interactions, they inadequately capture the concurrent nature of multi-interest behaviors and fail to model the underlying multi-centric distribution of user intent. To tackle this issue, we propose OT-FlowRec, an optimal transport-guided multi-bridge flow matching framework that explicitly models multi-interest distributions to facilitate multimodal sequential recommendation. Unlike single-path generative models, OT-FlowRec constructs a mixture of parallel, interest-specific transport flows to model the multi-centric distribution characteristics, where each flow preserves a distinct user interest cluster via an optimal transport plan. Then, a geometric transport mechanism is designed to establish minimum-cost paths from the latent multi-interest distribution to target preference prototypes to provide multi-interest awareness. Moreover, a progressive time-sampling warmup strategy dynamically biases optimization weights toward the final states of the generation process, bridging the gap between continuous global distribution fitting and practical top-$k$ ranking metrics. This approach achieves explicit interest disentanglement, ensuring the preservation of a multi-peaked preference representation instead of collapsing it into a unimodal average. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that OT-FlowRec outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines.

Multimedia.title: PhysElite: How Far Are LLMs from Solving Olympiad-Level Physics Problems?
Multimedia.summary: Understanding how (multimodal) large language models perform on physics problems requires benchmarks that reflect the difficulty and breadth of expert-level physical reasoning. Existing physics benchmarks remain limited in the following two important ways: (1) short of high-difficulty datasets, and (2) lack of comprehensive coverage of visual forms, knowledge points, and step-by-step solution processes. As a result, model performance on current datasets may not be fully representative of their ability to solve complex physics problems. To address these issues, we present PhysElite, a large-scale bilingual multimodal benchmark for Olympiad-level physics reasoning. PhysElite contains 11,586 Olympiad-tier problems. For each problem, we provide corresponding visual diagrams, step-by-step bilingual Chinese-English solution derivations, and the final answer. We benchmark 18 open-source and closed-source MLLMs, and find that even the strongest model reaches only 33.7% answer accuracy. We additionally conduct step-level process evaluation to diagnose where models fail in the reasoning chain. Our datasets are released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/physelite/PhysElite.
Multimedia.comment: Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2026

Multimedia.title: World-T3: Test-Time Training as Persistent Memory for Real-Time Video World Models
Multimedia.summary: Recent advances in video world models have enabled plausible interactive environments, yet long-horizon generation places a fundamental demand on visual memory: the previously observed world must remain consistent as the model continues to generate. Existing autoregressive approaches often implicitly rely on the generative model itself to retain such information, leading to spatial memory decay beyond the active context. We introduce World-T3, a camera-controlled video world model with a test-time training memory that consolidates past observations into dedicated model parameters. To robustly update this memory, we propose a recursive least-squares rule that incrementally absorbs novel visual features via online pose-keyed memory updates. Our TTT memory reads out previously observed scene features from the fast-weight state by camera pose, enabling consistent generation with constant storage and per-step computation regardless of rollout length. To facilitate real-time interactive generation with this robust memory, we further distill the autoregressive model into a few-step generator via dual-teacher distribution matching. On a long-horizon revisit benchmark, World-T3 raises revisit PSNR from 13.52 to 18.31 dB and reduces absolute rotation error from 3.344 to 1.075 relative to the strongest baseline on both metrics, while sustaining 20.6 FPS at 1280 x 704 on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU.
Multimedia.comment: Project Page: https://adreamwu.github.io/World-T3/

Multimedia.title: GHOST: Geometry-Constrained Hybrid Diffusion for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation
Multimedia.summary: 3D scene graph generation requires understanding both object semantics and metric spatial relations. However, existing open-vocabulary methods often struggle with spatial predicates because language similarity reflects semantic co-occurrence rather than explicit geometry. We propose GHOST, a Geometry-constrained Hybrid diffusion framework for Open-vocabulary 3D Scene graph generaTion. GHOST jointly models continuous node geometry and discrete edge predicates, following a geometry-to-constraint-to-predicate denoising process to ensure geometrically consistent relation prediction. It introduces language-grounded constraint induction, which maps predicate embeddings to differentiable geometric constraints that guide both layout refinement and predicate reweighting. A Geometry-Topology Collaborative Denoiser further couples node and edge reasoning through noise-adaptive interaction and orientation-aware modeling. Experiments on 3DSSG demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both closed-set and open-vocabulary settings, including over 17-point gains over RelationField on spatial predicates.
Multimedia.comment: 10 pages. Accepted at ACM MM 2026 (34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia)

Multimedia.title: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding
Multimedia.summary: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong results on video question answering, yet often fail to recover the temporal structure that makes a video coherent. They may merge neighboring events, miss single-event progression, or infer implausible relations across events. We study structured temporal understanding as the ability to recover event structure from visual evidence, including event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations. We argue that this gap arises from a mismatch between current post-training objectives and temporal reasoning, where caption-style supervision allows models to rely on language shortcuts rather than visual temporal grounding. To address this, we propose EventLens, a vision-centric reinforcement learning framework that learns video understanding through event-structure recovery. Instead of reconstructing captions, EventLens trains models to recover temporal structure under controlled perturbations, such as altered temporal granularity, reversed progression, and shuffled event order. We instantiate this framework with a three-level temporal ontology and derive three verifiable task families: event segmentation, progression discrimination, and multi-event relation reasoning. These tasks admit deterministic rewards, enabling task-specialized GRPO training without human preference labels or learned reward models. We further introduce multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MT-OPD) to consolidate specialized policies into a unified model. Experiments on Qwen3-VL backbones show consistent improvements on temporal grounding and event-sensitive reasoning benchmarks, while preserving general video-QA performance. Learning curves further demonstrate that EventLens achieves comparable downstream transfer with significantly reduced training cost compared to direct mixed RL optimization.
Multimedia.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, 13 tables. Project page: https://lostgreen.github.io/EventLens/

Multimedia.title: Elephant in the Fridge: Constant-Memory Frame Packing for Long Video Understanding
Multimedia.summary: Hour-long videos, streaming feeds, and movie-length content are pushing vision-language models (VLMs) past their breaking point -- the standard recipe of encoding each frame into visual tokens yields sequences that grow linearly with video length, causing prohibitive memory consumption and inference latency. Existing approaches, such as token reduction and keyframe selection, shorten the token sequence but leave the O(n) scaling intact, failing to resolve the fundamental bottleneck. We propose FramePack-U, a strikingly simple, training-free frame packing framework that compresses arbitrarily long videos into a fixed size visual representation at constant memory cost. FramePack-U requires no fine-tuning or architectural modification -- it plugs directly into off-the-shelf VLMs at inference time. Inspired by FramePack from the generation literature, we propose a content-aware compression strategy for visual understanding under a fixed token budget. Specifically, FramePack-U (1) scores each frame by its semantic similarity to the text prompt and ranks frames in a diversity-driven manner, and (2) packs the selected frames at varying resolutions into a fixed-length context window. This concentrates the memory budget on frames that are both instruction-relevant and visually diverse. While FramePack-U can in theory pack arbitrarily many frames into the fixed budget, we identify an empirical instantiation that generalizes robustly across settings. Extensive experiments on LongVideoBench, MLVU, and Video-MME show that FramePack-U consistently outperforms full-resolution baselines and prior token reduction and keyframe selection methods across diverse model families, parameter scales, and frame budgets. Notably, on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with a 128-frame budget, FramePack-U yields gains of +12.9\%, +10.6\%, and +9.7\% over the official model on the three benchmarks, respectively.
Multimedia.comment: NeurIPS 2026 (https://zeld0n.github.io/framepack-U/)

Multimedia.title: Toward Generative Video Communication: A Dual-Stream Digital Transmission Framework
Multimedia.summary: Generative video communication has shown promise for bandwidth-constrained wireless transmission and has the potential to support personalized content delivery. In this article, we propose a dual-stream digital generative video communication (DGVC) framework that integrates a traditional digital link with a generative link. The traditional link provides source-grounded visual references, while the generative link conveys compact semantic and perceptual information for receiver-side generation. We further discuss three bandwidth-dependent operating regimes and key technologies for dual-stream coordination, synchronization, reliability, and latency control. A practical case study demonstrates the perceptual and temporal-quality benefits of DGVC under wireless fading channels. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions for generative video communication.
Multimedia.comment: Following further technical review, we have identified limitations in the design of the proposed framework

Multimedia.title: JSIR: An Audio-Aligned, Multi-Task Dataset of Jazz Standard Recordings
Multimedia.summary: Beat tracking, chord estimation, and structure analysis are staple tasks of music information retrieval. Their datasets are drawn largely from Western popular music, and jazz remains a repertoire on which state-of-the-art systems underperform. We present JSIR, the Jazz Standards dataset for Information Retrieval. Its 267 recordings of 44 jazz standards span 25.6 hours, 3.7 times the audio of JAAH, the closest existing resource. For each recording, we provide annotations for beat and downbeat positions, chords, and sections, all produced by a jazz musician and revised in several passes. In baseline experiments, models trained with JSIR also improve on other jazz datasets: the downbeat F-measure of a state-of-the-art beat tracker rises from 87.7% to 89.2%, and the seventh-chord accuracy of a pop-trained chord estimator on JAAH from 34% to 41%. We publicly release the annotations, the annotation tool used to create them, and a web application that displays them in sync with the audio.
Multimedia.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027; 5 pages, 1 figure

Multimedia.title: SIMPLE: Semantic Structure-Aligned Prompt Learning for Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization
Multimedia.summary: Open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization aims to infer explicit segment-level categories for both seen and unseen audio-visual events. Existing solutions rely heavily on hand-crafted prompt templates, whose predictions are highly sensitive to subtle wording variations. Learnable prompts remove this manual tuning burden, but when trained solely on seen events, they tend to overfit to seen categories and distort the inter-event semantic topology required for generalization to unseen categories, a failure we term semantic topology drift. In this paper, we propose SIMPLE, a semantic structure-aligned prompt learning framework that aligns cross-category semantic topology between learnable and hand-crafted prompts across asynchronous audio and visual streams. Specifically, our SIMPLE combines Learnable Continuous Prompt Tuning (LCPT) with Semantic Topology Consistency Regularization (STCR). The LCPT automates prompt engineering through data-driven optimization, while the STCR module aligns the category-wise similarity distributions of learnable and hand-crafted prompts under random category subset sampling to alleviate semantic topology drift. Comprehensive experiments and analyses on the OV-AVEBench demonstrate that our SIMPLE framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the seen and unseen splits, while using roughly half the trainable parameters and roughly one-third the training time.

Multimedia.title: PAG-Agent: Zero-Shot Personalized Music Album Generation via Aesthetic Profile Distillation
Multimedia.summary: Large Music Models (LMMs) can synthesize high-fidelity audio and support increasingly flexible prompt control, yet modeling the subjective preferences of an individual listener remains underexplored. We present PAG-Agent, a zero-shot multimodal framework that uses an explicit Personal Aesthetic Profile to bridge user preference inference and music generation control. A multimodal LLM distills favorite-song audio and contextual user information into this structured representation, which a planning LLM translates into generation instructions for existing music synthesizers. We further introduce PA-Eval, which evaluates personalization through the Aesthetic Consistency Score (ACS) for target-user alignment and the Aesthetic Specificity Index (ASI) for cross-user specificity. Experiments with Personal-100 on multiple MLLM and music-generation backbones show consistent improvements over generic and direct conditioning. A 50-participant follow-up study further shows a correlation $r=0.64$ between ACS and subjective preference.
Multimedia.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures

Multimedia.title: Multi-agent Undercover Gaming: Hallucination Removal via Counterfactual Test for Multimodal Reasoning
Multimedia.summary: Hallucination continues to pose a major obstacle in the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Although the Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) paradigm offers a promising solution by promoting consensus among multiple agents to enhance reliability, it relies on the unrealistic assumption that all debaters are rational and reflective, which is a condition that may not hold when agents themselves are prone to hallucinations. To address this gap, we introduce the Multi-agent Undercover Gaming (MUG) protocol, inspired by social deduction games like "Who is Undercover?". MUG reframes MAD as a process of detecting "undercover" agents (those suffering from hallucinations) by employing multimodal counterfactual tests. Specifically, we modify reference images to introduce counterfactual evidence and observe whether agents can accurately identify these changes, providing ground-truth for identifying hallucinating agents and enabling robust, crowd-powered multimodal reasoning. MUG advances MAD protocols along three key dimensions: (1) enabling factual verification beyond statistical consensus through counterfactual testing; (2) introducing cross-evidence reasoning via dynamically modified evidence sources instead of relying on static inputs; and (3) fostering active reasoning, where agents engage in probing discussions rather than passively answering questions. Collectively, these innovations offer a more reliable and effective framework for multimodal reasoning in LLMs. The source code can be accessed at https://github.com/YongLD/MUG.git.
Multimedia.comment: Accepted by AAAI 2026

Multimedia.title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
Multimedia.summary: Explainer videos -- a worked geometry problem, why the sky is blue, how a dynasty fell -- are usually one more target for pixel video generation. We argue they are a different kind of artifact: a program (script, storyboard and per-frame animation code) that a deterministic renderer turns into frames. A program can be read, diffed, tested and audited; pixels can only be watched. Reels-RSI is an open-source reel director for any agent harness; its self-improvement happens at the program level rather than in weights or prompts. Every revision pass is logged with a code snapshot; a retrospective pairs each check finding with the diff that fixed it and proposes lessons; a lesson that a static check can catch is compiled into a rule with a must-fail and a must-pass example, so the memory is unit-tested; and a rule learned today runs over everything made before it. A bounded, benchmark-gated step lets an agent rewrite the director's playbook, kept only when blind pairwise judgments on held-out topics prefer it; nothing enters memory without a human decision. Across 111 reels -- a field study, two playbook evolutions, a 2x2 memory ablation, a weaker director, a 48-reel learning curve and a judge-reliability study -- we find that the rule learned in the field caught four latent defects in frames authored before it existed and none after; that rules are an audit for a strong director (eight unguarded reels, no violation) and a guard for a weaker one (thirty violations unguarded versus five); that lessons shorten revision loops but do not compound or move the judge; and that the first rewrite's 11--1 verdict was a position bias in our vote design (judges pick the second-shown reel 62--81% of the time), masking scripts that traded thirteen facts for craft. We document four failure modes of the preference signal, which check caught each, and the fixes. Code, rules, lessons and data are public.
Multimedia.comment: 19 pages, 4 figures, 9 tables. Code, rules, lessons, data and evolve reports: https://github.com/agentic-loops-x/Reels-RSI

Multimedia.title: DIA: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Interest-Aware ABR Scheme for Cloud Gaming
Multimedia.summary: The continuous evolution of cloud gaming has enabled users to play high-quality cloud games on thin clients, such as smartphones and tablets. However, how to effectively transmit the gameplay frames with high resolution and low latency, especially over wireless networks, remains a significant challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based Interest-Aware Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) scheme, called DIA, that guarantees the quality of perceptually key objects in each frame, while dynamically allocating lower resolutions for non-key objects to conserve bandwidth under constrained network conditions. By leveraging an off-the-shelf semantic segmentation model, the proposed DIA scheme can adjust the bitrate at the object-level. We also design a transformer-based feature extractor and an interest-aware reward function to enable the proposed DIA scheme to identify key objects and dynamically adjust their bitrates. This adaptation is guided by users' in-game movement speed, object features, and prevailing network conditions and operates without requiring additional hardware, such as gaze trackers. Extensive experiments show that the proposed DIA scheme outperforms existing ABR schemes in dynamic wireless network environments. Notably, DIA achieves at least a 20% higher normalized average Quality of Experience (QoE) than the State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) ABR algorithms in 5G scenarios.

Multimedia.title: EmoGavel: Grounding-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for Multimodal Emotion Preference Learning
Multimedia.summary: Multimodal emotion preference learning uses pairwise comparisons to identify which open-ended emotion descriptions align more closely with human judgments. However, existing methods primarily focus on the final preference decision and provide little explicit supervision for localizing and correcting erroneous content. To address this limitation, we propose EmoGavel, a Grounding-Aware reinforcement learning framework with Verifiable rewards for multimodal Emotion preference Learning. We first introduce grounded supervised fine-tuning (Grounded SFT), which exploits controlled-error construction information to jointly learn preference prediction, error localization, repair, and missing-evidence recovery. We then optimize these verifiable outcomes with grounding-aware group relative policy optimization (GA-GRPO), combining preference-gated grounding rewards with dynamic zero-variance rescue to prioritize preference correctness and recover learning signals from all-wrong groups. Experiments on EmoPrefer and controlled-error evaluation sets show that EmoGavel improves both natural preference prediction and controlled-error discrimination while maintaining strong error-grounding performance. Our code and model checkpoints will be released once the paper is accepted.

Multimedia.title: CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation
Multimedia.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) reveals versatility and convenience during VLM post-training, providing dense supervision for student from teacher. However, we observed an anomaly that the distilled VLM could still answer the questions accurately even when the related visual regions were masked or replaced with noise. Building on this observation, our quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that OPD, which uses the answer as a hint, has failed to teach students to genuinely seek out and rely on visual evidence. Our theoretical analysis suggests that this failure arises from a shortcut enabled by the lack of visual constraints during distillation. To address the issue, we introduce Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation (CV-OPD), which compares teacher distributions induced by positive and negative crops while conditioning on the same student prefix and augments optimization with a margin-based contrastive constraint, which is modulated with discrepancy gating across token and sample level. Specifically, CV-OPD first introduces a negative teacher unrelated to the answer and designs a Contrastive Divergence Loss (CDL) that constrains the feature distribution of student by contrasting the positive and negative teachers, correcting how the student exploits visual regions. The CV-OPD introduces a Discrepancy Aware Gate (DAG) that uses token-level and sample-level discrepancies to select visually relevant tokens for optimization, directing the student's attention toward visual content. Extensive experiments across a broad range of fine-grained visual benchmarks demonstrate that CV-OPD substantially alleviates shortcut and consistently improves the visual reasoning capabilities of existing VLMs.
Multimedia.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, contrastive learning for on-policy distillation of VLMs. Computer Vision. Post-training. VLM. LLM

Multimedia.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
Multimedia.summary: Video editing models achieve strong performance in modifying appearance, backgrounds, styles, and motions, empowered by large-scale training data. Beyond general scenarios, professional motions are significant in performance, sports, and martial arts. This paper focuses on professional motion editing, which involves fine-grained motion technique and temporal structure. Given professional motion names but lacking detailed descriptions, existing models often fail to generate professional motions, such as incorrectly lifting the front wheel under a Stoppie instruction. To address this challenge, we introduce MotionCoach, a trained multimodal agent that uses multi-turn tools and performs self-verification, producing a grounded prompt and a reference clip as reliable and sufficient multimodal guidance to inject external professional motion knowledge into video editing models. To supply training data, we build a data pipeline to construct trajectories. We cold-start the agent on MotionCoach-SFT-10k and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on MotionCoach-RL-2k with rewards on the motion guidance prompt, the motion outcome video, and the format. For evaluation, we introduce VPMEBench, comprising 314 professional motion editing tasks with fine-grained references and annotations. Extensive experiments show that MotionCoach improves the overall score from 55.1 to 65.6 on Seedance 2.0 and from 51.2 to 64.5 on MiniMax-H3. Learning to construct multimodal guidance enables precise professional motion editing without retraining video editing models.
